content.title: About
content.content: Luncheon meat, loaf type (1013) is a solid, fully cooked meat product formed into a loaf shape. It is made from selected meat cuts (usually pork and beef), salt, spices and often includes curing agents such as nitrites to preserve color and extend shelf life.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “loaf” refers to the bread‑like shape of the product.
In many post‑Soviet countries this product is commonly called “meat loaf” or simply “loaf”.
It is a popular base for sandwiches, cold platters and salads.
Flavor enhancers like garlic, paprika or mustard powder are sometimes added.
The solid form makes it easy to slice thinly for school cafeterias and catering.

items.title: Source of high‑quality protein
items.content: Provides essential animal protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Provides heme iron, which is readily absorbed and supports oxygen transport.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Supplies B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Contribute to bone and dental health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The product is often heavily salted, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Some additives can cause allergic reactions or increase the formation of nitrosamines with long‑term consumption.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: May contain significant saturated fat, a consideration for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Individuals with specific meat allergies should avoid it.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the loaf thinly for sandwiches, salads, snack platters or enjoy it as a quick bite. It can be served cold or gently warmed in a pan or microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C in the original packaging or an airtight container. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C or below.
